name: Alzirr
description: A naked-eye star 18.0 parsecs away, 2.7 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 48737: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.401 +/- 0.009 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 2.71 +/- 0.021

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 48737: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.706 +/- 0.012

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 48737: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6480 +/- 39

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3352485999058854912 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 48737: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 55.55 +/- 0.19 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 18 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 2.7 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.401 milliarcseconds, which gives 2.71 solar radii and 6,480 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 48737: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
